subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — uptime & latency commitments
messages:

Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com

Subject: Procurement questionnaire — uptime & latency commitments

Hi Connor,

Thanks for taking our procurement packet. Our security and procurement teams have a couple of specific follow-ups focused on service commitments. Could you please provide short, specific answers to the items below so we can complete our vendor review?

1) What uptime/availability commitment do you make for the hosted API? Please list the SLA target and the measurement window.
2) How is latency SLO defined (p50/p95/p99), and what measurement methodology do you use (request-level, synthetic probes, sampling)?
3) Do customers get read-only access to the real-time or historical metrics dashboards? If so, what metrics are visible and how are they scoped by account/team?
4) What is your incident/exception process for scheduled maintenance or capacity degradations that exceed SLOs? How are credits calculated and applied?
5) What logs/telemetry will be included in an audit package (latency histograms, outage timelines, root cause summaries)?

We appreciate succinct answers and any attachments. If you prefer a quick call with SRE to walk through, let us know windows tomorrow.

Best,
Jenny
Procurement — Acme Corp
From: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.inference>
To: Jenny Lee <j.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-05-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — uptime & latency commitments

Jenny —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together answers below and attached a short SLO definition doc and metrics access instructions. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with our SRE lead if you'd like a walk-through.

1) Uptime SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime for the Redwood hosted inference API (control plane and inference endpoints measured together). Measurement window: rolling 30-day period. Credits: tiered credit schedule (0.5%–2.5% credit tiers) — see attachment for the exact table.

2) Latency SLOs and measurement: Latency SLOs are defined per-route and per-model. Default public SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 450ms on our X-series GPU instances for small/medium payloads. Measurement methodology: request-level aggregation across production traffic (sampling rate 1:1 for authenticated tenant traffic), with synthetic probe coverage for cross-region baselining. We compute latency histograms over 1-minute buckets and roll up to hourly and daily summaries.

3) Customer access to metrics: Yes — customers receive read-only access to a scoped metrics dashboard via the Redwood Console. Visible metrics include: request rate (RPS), token throughput, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), error rate, and cache hit ratio. Dashboards can be scoped by API key or by dedicated capacity pool. Historical retention: 90 days by default; extended retention is an add-on.

4) Exception & maintenance process: Planned maintenance is notified 72 hours in advance with a maintenance ticket; brief maintenance windows (<30 minutes) are excluded from SLA calculations if pre-notified. Unplanned degradations: we triage, issue status updates via the Console incident feed and email, and follow the SLA credit table if rolling 30-day uptime falls below thresholds. Credits are pro rata applied to the following billing cycle after verification. For Dedicated/Private customers, we will negotiate tailored exception terms in enterprise agreements.

5) Audit artifacts: We provide latency histograms, outage timelines, incident postmortems (P0/P1), and a telemetry export (request-level aggregates, not raw request bodies) as part of an audit package. Sensitive content (payloads) is excluded; log sampling is configurable.

Attachments: redwood-slo-definition.pdf (SLA table + examples), metrics-access-instructions.md (how to grant read-only access).

If useful, looping in our SRE lead @karthik_iyer for technical detail. Are you available 11am–1pm PT tomorrow for a short call?

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.inference>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-05-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Procurement questionnaire — uptime & latency commitments

Connor/Marissa — forwarding brief notes for the call. High-level points to highlight to Acme:

- Measurement: emphasize we calculate per-tenant latency percentiles from production request-level telemetry; sampling is full (no tail-sampling) for authenticated customer traffic so p99s are meaningful.
- Dashboards: show them that metrics can be scoped by API key and by model/deployment; we can add a custom dashboard for Acme during onboarding.
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance <30m is excluded if notified 72h; for any extended capacity issues we implement temporary routing to a compatible model variant with documented performance trade-offs.
- Credits: we validate with telemetry exports and incident timelines before applying credits; sometimes customers request one-off exceptions for business-impacting events — route those to legal/sales for review.

I'll be on the call and can share a short live query to demonstrate p99 histograms and the 30-day uptime calculation.

-karthik
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

Jenny —

Thanks again for the questions and the time on the call earlier today. Quick follow-ups from our side:

- We shared a live demo of the metrics view and the p99 histogram (recording link: https://console.redwood.ai/metrics/ACME-123).
- For audit deliverables, we'll prepare a trimmed telemetry export and an incident timeline document; expect those within 3 business days after contract signature or upon your request for a one-time audit.
- Exception requests: if Acme needs a contractual SLA exception (for e.g., guaranteed p99 lower than public SLOs), we can accept a written exception request and route it through Legal for evaluation. Exceptions are scoped by product region and capacity commitment.

Next steps: I will attach the final SLO doc to the SoW and post the metrics read-only invite for your team by EOD. If you need the DocuSign for the exception appendix, confirm and I'll trigger it.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive
